title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of the 19-page set 'Catégorie de Galois-Teichmüller d'un corps alg. clos'. Grothendieck sets up a topological 'isotopy category' of surfaces.

Objects: connected, oriented, topological surfaces of finite type, i.e. a compact surface minus finitely many points.

Morphisms (1): Hom_isot(X,Y) is the set of path components of the space of finite étale maps X -> Y, that is, finite-degree covering maps. He struck out the restriction 'respectant l'orientation'.

Isotopy (2)-(3): two finite étale maps f, g : X -> Y lie in the same component iff there is a continuous family F : X×I -> Y×I over I with F_0 = f and F_1 = g.

Factorisation (4)-(5): F is a finite covering of Y×I. Coverings of Y×I come uniquely from coverings of Y (pull-back along Y×I -> Y), because Y×I retracts onto Y. So there is a finite étale cover p : Y' -> Y, unique up to unique isomorphism, and a homeomorphism α : X×I -> Y'×I over I with F = (p×id_I)∘α.

Consequence (next page): f and g are isotopic iff f = p∘f_0 and g = p∘g_0 with f_0, g_0 : X -> Y' isotopic homeomorphisms. Equivalently g = f∘u with u a homeomorphism of X isotopic to the identity. Hence Hom_isot(X,Y) = {finite coverings X -> Y}/Homeo_0(X).

Purpose: this defines a category whose automorphism groups are (extended) mapping class groups and whose morphisms are isotopy classes of finite coverings. It is the topological model on which Gal(Q̄/Q) is meant to act, via an algebraic/profinite counterpart over an algebraically closed field: the 'Galois-Teichmüller category'.
errors: Grothendieck invokes only full faithfulness of Y' |-> Y'×I. Existence of Y' and α (given F) needs essential surjectivity, i.e. that every finite covering of Y×I is pulled back from Y. This is true by homotopy invariance of coverings, so the functor is in fact an equivalence; the gap is minor.
He tacitly uses that F, a fibrewise family of finite coverings, is itself a finite covering of Y×I. This holds (properness plus local homeomorphism, via invariance of domain), but it is not argued.
The topology on the mapping space (presumably compact-open) is not specified; 'composantes connexes' is corrected to 'par arcs', which is the right notion for isotopy.

ideas.what: Category of finite-type surfaces with morphisms = isotopy classes of finite étale (covering) maps; Aut = mapping class groups
ideas.modern_name: Category of surfaces and finite coverings up to isotopy (tower of mapping class groups under coverings; commensurator-type structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Grothendieck's Esquisse d'un programme (1984) Teichmüller tower; developed later by Ihara, Drinfeld (GT), Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Boggi and others in profinite/étale form
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche discuss Teichmüller groupoids and π1 of surfaces; this exact 'catégorie isotopique' with covering morphisms is not, to my knowledge, spelled out there

ideas.what: Isotopy of coverings factors through a fixed intermediate cover: f ~ g iff g = f∘u with u isotopic to id
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy invariance of coverings / lifting of isotopies through finite covers

missed.claim: The opening of a dedicated 19-page construction of a 'Galois-Teichmüller category' for an algebraically closed field, whose topological prototype is the isotopy category of surfaces with finite coverings as morphisms (not only homeomorphisms and degenerations as in the Esquisse tower). This category-level packaging, with covering morphisms included, is a variant less emphasised in the published Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature.
missed.quote: Hom_isot(X,Y) = ensemble des composantes par arcs connexes de l'espace des applications finies étales de X dans Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Including covering morphisms links the GT/Teichmüller tower to commensurability and congruence-subgroup questions for mapping class groups (Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki) and to anabelian geometry of curves. Seeing how Grothendieck intended Galois to act on this category could be of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine setup: definitions and a standard covering-space argument. Interest lies only in its being the start of an early (from 1978) explicit 'Galois-Teichmüller category' that includes finite coverings as morphisms; the mathematics on this page itself is classical.
transcription_corrections: The heading '1' and the margin '2' are the manuscript page number and the archive page index; they are not equation labels.

The inserted phrase above 'définissent' reads 'sont isotopes i.e.', and the struck word after it is 'applicat[ion]'. The line should read 'f et g sont isotopes i.e. définissent la même composante...'.
The struck text before '(2)' is an aborted 'F de X×I', correctly marked as deleted.
